summary: Full backend + frontend testing of SteelBiz. Backend: 28/28 pytest tests pass covering auth, dashboard, CRUD (customers/suppliers/products/coils), purchase→inventory increase, sale→inventory decrease + profit calc + PDF invoice, payments reducing outstanding, all 6 report kinds, all 5 CSV/JSON exports, and AI Ask with follow-up. Frontend: PIN login (wrong+correct), dashboard KPIs (all 7) + range filters, create Customer/Supplier/Product via UI, create Sale (Ravi Traders/GI Pipe) and Purchase (JSW/GI Pipe), Ask My Business Q&A with maintained follow-up context (correctly identified Ravi Traders as buyer of PPGL Roofing Sheet with real numbers from DB). Discovered and fixed a critical React bug: 6 pages used `useEffect(load, [])` where load returns a Promise, causing a Red-screen `TypeError: destroy is not a function` overlay on unmount that blocked Customers, Suppliers, Payments, Purchases and Sales pages during navigation. Fixed by wrapping in arrow function `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [])` in all 6 pages.

ui_bugs.issue: useEffect(load, []) passed a Promise-returning function to React causing 'TypeError: destroy is not a function' red overlay on navigation/unmount, blocking all interactions with these pages

action_items: Verify the useEffect fix in 6 pages is acceptable (Customers.js, Suppliers.js, Inventory.js, Payments.js, Purchases.js, Sales.js)

Consider adopting a proper React data-fetching pattern (SWR/react-query) or an explicit `useEffect(() => { let ok=true; api.get(...).then(r => ok && setX(r.data)); return () => { ok=false; }; }, [])` for cancellation safety.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1100+ lines: consider splitting into routers (auth, customers, suppliers, products, sales, purchases, analytics, reports).

customer_outstanding double-counts payments: it adds `sum(payments.amount)` AND `sum(sales.amount_paid)` — if a shopkeeper records amount_paid inside the sale AND then creates a Payment record for the same money, outstanding will be understated. Suggest documenting which source of truth to use.
apply_sale_to_inventory allows negative stock without validation (new_qty = old_qty - qty is written even if negative). Consider guarding.

apply_sale_to_inventory: unbound local `cost` when product not found (`it['_cost'] = cost if prod else 0` — `cost` may reference variable from previous iteration). Not caught in tests because seed data has all products.
Login: `pin.length >= 8` cap but backend requires >=4. Fine, but there is no rate-limit/lockout on PIN attempts — brute-forceable in 10^4 = 10000 tries.
CORS default is '*' with allow_credentials=True — invalid per spec; browsers will reject credentialed requests. In this deployment REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL matches host so OK, but the config is fragile.
Frontend uses localStorage token (JWT) — vulnerable to XSS token theft. httpOnly cookie recommended.
Scan endpoints upload to object storage without try/finally cleanup on failure of storage; low priority.

success_rate.frontend: 100% after useEffect fix (all critical flows: login, dashboard, customer/supplier/product create, sale, purchase, ask+follow-up)

seed_data_creation: Backend test flow creates TEST_ prefixed customer/supplier/product/purchase/sale and cleans them up. UI test left a few TEST_UI_* records (customer/supplier/product) plus 1 sale on Ravi Traders (GI Pipe x2 @100) and 1 purchase on JSW (GI Pipe x10 @80).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fully green. Frontend useEffect(load, []) pattern was a bug across 6 pages — fixed. If retesting, log in with PIN 112233 and note that seed data plus test-created rows exist. Product 'TEST_Flow' was created by backend test with 90KG stock at cost 100. AI Ask endpoint takes ~5-10s per call.
rca of the issue: Root cause: `useEffect(load, [])` where `const load = () => api.get(...).then(...)` — the arrow expression returns the Promise from api.get().then(). React interprets the return value as a cleanup function. On unmount (route navigation) React calls `destroy()` on that Promise, throwing `TypeError: destroy is not a function` and triggering the red DEV overlay that visually blocked buttons. Repro: log in, click Customers in the nav → red overlay covers page; buttons unreachable. Mitigation: wrap in a block-returning arrow so the effect returns undefined: `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [])`. Applied to Customers.js, Suppliers.js, Inventory.js, Payments.js, Purchases.js, Sales.js.
